grounded_facts: Rogozhin formally extends an invitation for Holmes to meet Madame Petrova privately after the performance.
memories.memory_text: I was present when Rogozhin formally invited me to meet Madame Petrova after the performance, mentioning she was expecting me in her dressing room.

grounded_facts: Watson humorously compliments the ballerinas' 'lovely po-pos' while patting them with his cane, after confirming they don't understand English.
memories.memory_text: I saw Watson check if the ballerinas understood English before telling them they had lovely po-pos, then patting them with his cane in a playful way.

grounded_facts: Holmes accepts the invitation to meet Madame Petrova after the performance, indicating willingness to take on her case despite lack of initial details.
memories.memory_text: I accepted Rogozhin's invitation to see Madame Petrova, and I followed him backstage, indicating my willingness to look into her matter despite not knowing the details yet.

grounded_facts: A backstage gathering after the show, featuring food, drink, and socializing among cast and crew, where Holmes is summoned to meet Petrova.
memories.memory_text: After the show, I was led through the backstage gathering—where Watson amused himself among the dancers—toward Petrova's dressing room as Rogozhin informed me she was expecting me.

grounded_facts: Petrova visually assesses Holmes from head to toe after their initial greeting.
memories.memory_text: I noticed Petrova appraising me from head to toe after we greeted each other.

grounded_facts: Petrova gifts Holmes a Stradivarius violin as a token of appreciation for services to be rendered.
memories.memory_text: I received a Stradivarius violin as a gift from Petrova through Rogozhin, who said it was from her as a token for services to be rendered.

grounded_facts: Petrova reveals she is retiring from ballet to focus on motherhood.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Rogozhin that Petrova is retiring from ballet to focus on motherhood.

grounded_facts: Watson briefly enters the dressing room, drunk and festive, asking about the meaning of 'prokanzik'.
memories.memory_text: I remember Watson stumbling into the dressing room, drunk and cheerful with a flower behind his ear, asking what 'prokanzik' meant before Rogozhin told him it meant 'You little devil' and he laughed and hurried off.

grounded_facts: Holmes indirectly reveals his romantic relationship with Dr. Watson to decline Petrova's proposal.
Holmes refuses Petrova's proposal to father her child, citing his relationship with Watson and sexual orientation.
memories.memory_text: I told Petrova I was not a free man because of my relationship with Watson, and when she asked if I meant us, I confirmed it with a quiet 'if you want to be picturesque about it,' making clear I could not father her child.

grounded_facts: A private celebration following Petrova's final ballet performance, held in her dressing room and extending into a larger party.
memories.memory_text: I witnessed a private celebration in Petrova's dressing room after her final performance, which later grew into a wild party with music, dancing, and drinking.

grounded_facts: Holmes tries to get Watson to leave the party, but Watson refuses and continues dancing.
memories.memory_text: I approached Watson at the party and told him it was time for us to go home, but he refused and kept dancing with the girls while I was left standing there.

grounded_facts: Watson is gradually abandoned by female dance partners, learns that a rumor about his romantic relationship with Holmes has spread, and reacts emotionally by drinking Rogozhin's vodka.
memories.memory_text: I later realized that Watson had been abandoned by his dance partners and was left dancing only with the male performers, and though I wasn't there to see it, I can imagine how he must have felt when he realized the rumor about us had spread—enough to make him drink Rogozhin's vodka in one gulp.

grounded_facts: A calm night at Holmes's residence following an unusual adventure, marked by stillness and solitude.
memories.memory_text: I remember the stillness of the night after that peculiar adventure, how the quiet settled over 221B like a blanket, just as I took my seat in the wing chair.

grounded_facts: Holmes is back at 221B Baker Street, having changed into a smoking jacket and settling in for a quiet moment after the evening's events.
memories.memory_text: I changed out of my dinner coat into my smoking jacket and took a moment to relax with my pipe, savoring the calm after the evening's events.

grounded_facts: Holmes hears approaching footsteps and turns his head, indicating he knows who is coming.
memories.memory_text: I heard hurried footsteps approaching and turned my head, knowing exactly who it was.

grounded_facts: Holmes repositions the wing chair to face away from the door and dims the lamp, suggesting preparation for confrontation or concealment.
memories.memory_text: I repositioned the wing chair to face away from the door and dimmed the lamp, preparing for Watson's return.

grounded_facts: Watson repeatedly calls Holmes' name upon entering the flat, indicating urgency or need to locate him.
memories.memory_text: I heard Watson call my name urgently as he entered the flat, repeating it with clear concern.

grounded_facts: Watson realizes the figure in the chair is not Holmes but a mechanical device used for smoking, revealing Holmes' deception.
memories.memory_text: I saw Watson approach the chair, knock it aside, and discover the smoking machine on the floor, then watch as he realized I had been hiding in the corner, manipulating it.

grounded_facts: In fury, Watson throws the smoking machine to the floor after learning of Holmes' deception.
memories.memory_text: I saw Watson dash the smoking machine to the floor in a fury after learning the truth.

grounded_facts: Holmes steps out from a shadowy corner, admitting he used the machine to avoid Watson's anger, thus ending the pretense.
Holmes apologizes but justifies his actions by claiming he was avoiding a madwoman.
memories.memory_text: I stepped out from the shadows and told Watson I was truly sorry, but I had to use the machine to escape a madwoman without hurting her feelings.

grounded_facts: Watson confronts Holmes about a prank that led to damaging public rumors implying a romantic relationship between them.
memories.memory_text: I remember Watson confronting me about the prank that sparked damaging rumors about us, demanding to know what I was thinking and how I could do such a thing to him.

grounded_facts: Holmes downplays Watson's fears of scandal by suggesting St. Petersburg gossip is trivial.
memories.memory_text: I told Watson that any gossip about him in St. Petersburg would be trivial and not worth his concern.

grounded_facts: Watson expresses fear that false rumors of a romantic relationship will destroy his reputation and pension.
memories.memory_text: Watson told me he feared the rumors would ruin his reputation and even cost him his pension from the Fifth Northumberland Fusiliers.

grounded_facts: Watson angrily blames Holmes for spreading lies and humiliating him.
memories.memory_text: I recall Watson angrily blaming me for lying and humiliating him, shouting that he felt dishonored and disgraced because of the public fallout from my deception.

grounded_facts: Holmes draws attention to the flower behind Watson's ear, prompting Watson to discard it.
memories.memory_text: I pointed out the flower behind Watson's ear, and he removed it immediately.

grounded_facts: In a moment of panic, Watson suggests he and Holmes get married to quell gossip, later rejecting the idea.
memories.memory_text: Watson mentioned, in a moment of panic, that we might get married to stop the gossip, though he quickly dismissed the idea.

grounded_facts: Holmes admits to Watson that there have been women in his life, then clarifies that Watson is being presumptuous.
memories.memory_text: I told Watson yes, there have been women in my life, but I made it clear he was being presumptuous to assume anything from that.

grounded_facts: Watson asks Holmes if he has ever had relationships with women.
memories.memory_text: Watson asked me if I've ever had relationships with women, clearly hoping I'd say no so he wouldn't feel awkward.

grounded_facts: Watson asks Holmes about his romantic history, seeking reassurance about their reputations.
memories.memory_text: I remember Watson asking me a hesitant question about my romantic history, and I told him the answer was yes—but he was being presumptuous, which visibly disappointed him.

grounded_facts: Gabrielle is identified as a woman in her early thirties with a bruise on her temple, wet hair, wrapped in a blanket, wearing a wedding ring, and unable to recall who she is or why she was at the river.
memories.memory_text: I saw that the woman, Gabrielle, was in her early thirties, had wet hair, a bruise on her temple, was wrapped in a blanket, wore a wedding ring, and couldn't remember who she was or why she was in the river.

grounded_facts: Holmes asks Gabrielle why she came to 221B Baker Street, attempting to extract information about her intentions.
memories.memory_text: I asked the young lady what she wanted at this address, hoping to learn why she had come to 221B Baker Street, but she told me she did not remember.

grounded_facts: A cabbie delivers a mysterious wet and injured woman named Gabrielle to 221B Baker Street, claiming she was pulled from the river and had the address in her hand.
memories.memory_text: The cabbie told me he pulled the woman from the river near Westminster Bridge and found our address in her hand, which is why he brought her here.

grounded_facts: The cabbie insists on being paid two-and-six for transporting Gabrielle, threatening to abandon her otherwise.
memories.memory_text: I heard the cabbie demand two-and-six from us, threatening to throw her back in the river if we didn't pay.

grounded_facts: Watson pays the cabbie two-and-six for bringing Gabrielle to 221B, accepting responsibility for her.
memories.memory_text: I saw Watson take out some coins and hand them to the cabbie, accepting responsibility for her by paying the fare.

grounded_facts: A sudden late-night visit by a cabbie delivering an unconscious woman to 221B Baker Street, disrupting the quiet evening of Holmes and Watson.
memories.memory_text: I was playing the violin when the bell rang late at night, and Watson went to answer the door, which interrupted my music and brought in a cabbie with a woman wrapped in a blanket.

grounded_facts: Gabrielle is brought to Holmes and Watson's living room, suffering from a head injury, exposure, and shock after being found in or near the Thames.
memories.memory_text: I saw Watson bring Gabrielle into our living room and settle her by the fireplace, clearly suffering from a head injury and shock after being found near the Thames.

grounded_facts: Watson diagnoses Gabrielle with a concussion leading to temporary amnesia based on her head wound and mental state.
memories.memory_text: I heard Watson diagnose her with a concussion leading to temporary amnesia, based on the head wound and her mental state.

grounded_facts: Holmes deduces Gabrielle's nationality and origin by examining a label inside her dress collar that reads 'BAZAAR MODERN, Bruxelles'.
memories.memory_text: I examined the label inside her dress collar and saw it read 'BAZAAR MODERN, Bruxelles', which told me she was from Brussels, Belgium.

grounded_facts: Holmes removes Gabrielle's wedding ring and reads the engraving 'Gabrielle - Emile', identifying her name and her husband's name.
memories.memory_text: I removed her wedding ring and, using my magnifying glass, read the engraving 'Gabrielle - Emile', which gave me her name and her husband's name.

grounded_facts: Holmes aggressively questions Gabrielle about her name, husband, and events at the river, causing her to burst into sobs.
memories.memory_text: I pressed Gabrielle hard with questions about her name, her husband, and what happened at the river, and I saw her break into sobs right before my eyes.

grounded_facts: Watson intervenes to stop Holmes' harsh questioning, asserting that Gabrielle must not be distressed further.
memories.memory_text: I remember Watson stepping in and telling me to stop, saying he wouldn't allow me to keep questioning her in that state.

grounded_facts: Watson prepares a sleeping potion and administers it to Gabrielle, who is then taken to bed by Mrs. Hudson.
memories.memory_text: I saw Watson prepare a sleeping potion by stirring a spoonful of white powder from his medical bag into Gabrielle's tea, and then I heard him tell Mrs. Hudson to put her to bed in my room.

grounded_facts: A medical and investigative session in which Gabrielle is examined, diagnosed, and partially identified by Holmes and Watson.
memories.memory_text: I took part in the examination, where I found a label in her dress collar and examined her wedding ring, learning her name is Gabrielle and her husband's name is Emile, then suggested to Watson that we arrange for her to be taken to a hospital.

grounded_facts: Holmes suggests sending Gabrielle to a hospital, while Watson insists on keeping her for protection and treatment.
memories.memory_text: I suggested to Watson that we send Gabrielle to a hospital for proper medical attention, but he insisted she remain under his care and protection, arguing that she was in danger after an attempt on her life, and I made clear I wanted the case resolved quickly so we could be rid of her.

grounded_facts: Holmes examines a piece of cardboard showing green smudges, indicating ongoing analysis of evidence.
memories.memory_text: I was standing by the window at dawn, studying a piece of cardboard with green smudges, trying to make sense of the evidence.

grounded_facts: Holmes' bed has not been used, indicating he stayed awake through the night.
memories.memory_text: I stayed awake through the night, and my bed shows no sign of having been used.

grounded_facts: Holmes silently looks at Gabrielle sleeping in Watson's bed and then quietly closes the door.
memories.memory_text: I silently looked at Gabrielle sleeping in Watson's bed and then quietly closed the door.

grounded_facts: Gabrielle emerges from Watson's bedroom at dawn and approaches Holmes in his room, initiating an intimate encounter that turns into a coded revelation.
Gabrielle pretends emotional and physical longing for Holmes, using the guise of a romantic reunion to掩护 a hidden message, manipulating the situation for undisclosed purposes.
memories.memory_text: I was in my room at dawn when Gabrielle emerged from Watson's bedroom and approached me, calling me 'Emile' and embracing me as if we were lovers, urging me to come to bed with her despite knowing I would suspect deception.

grounded_facts: Holmes notices green ink letters on Gabrielle's palm and uses a mirror to reveal their reversed form as the number '301', indicating a concealed code.
memories.memory_text: I noticed green ink on Gabrielle's palm as she reached for me, and when I used my magnifying mirror to examine it, I saw the reflection revealed the number '301', clearly a hidden code.

grounded_facts: Watson discovers that Gabrielle is no longer in her bedroom, despite her clothes remaining.
memories.memory_text: I inferred that Gabrielle must have disappeared because her clothes were still in the bedroom, even though she was no longer there.

grounded_facts: Mrs. Hudson informs Watson that Gabrielle is no longer in her room.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Mrs. Hudson that Gabrielle was no longer in her room when she came to me shouting, 'Holmes! She's gone!'

grounded_facts: Mrs. Hudson checks on Gabrielle in her bedroom and discovers she is missing.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Mrs. Hudson that Gabrielle was gone.

grounded_facts: Watson shouts to alert Holmes that Gabrielle has disappeared.
memories.memory_text: I heard Watson shout at me that Gabrielle was gone.

grounded_facts: Watson prepares to enter Holmes' bedroom to alert him but freezes upon seeing something inside.
memories.memory_text: I saw Watson throw open my door and start to enter, but then he froze in place after seeing something inside.

grounded_facts: Holmes sarcastically tells Mrs. Hudson to wipe her disapproving expression, prompting her to leave angrily.
memories.memory_text: I told Mrs. Hudson to go to the kitchen and wipe that look of disapproval off her face, and she stormed out in a huff, muttering about liberties in her own house.

grounded_facts: Holmes enters the living room carrying Gabrielle Valladon's suitcase, which he has retrieved using a luggage ticket clue from her hand.
memories.memory_text: I entered the living room carrying Gabrielle Valladon's suitcase, which I retrieved using the luggage ticket clue that had transferred from her hand to the cardboard.

grounded_facts: Holmes uses a butter-knife to force open the locks of the suitcase and begins examining its contents.
memories.memory_text: I used a butter-knife to force open the locks of the suitcase and began examining its contents, including a pink negligee and a bundle of letters, with Watson observing.

grounded_facts: Holmes begins active investigation of Gabrielle Valladon's case by retrieving and examining her suitcase.
memories.memory_text: I began my active investigation of Gabrielle Valladon's case by retrieving her suitcase and opening it to examine the contents, including a bundle of letters I removed.

grounded_facts: Gabrielle emerges from Holmes's bedroom, confirms her identity as Gabrielle Valladon, and identifies the man in the photo as her husband, Emile Valladon.
memories.memory_text: I saw Gabrielle emerge from my bedroom wearing my dressing gown, unsteady and dazed, and I confirmed her identity by asking if she was Gabrielle Valladon, to which she replied yes; then I showed her a photo and asked if the man was her husband Emile Valladon, and she confirmed that as well.

grounded_facts: Holmes tells Gabrielle that Watson is the handsome one, causing Watson to smile and twirl his mustache.
memories.memory_text: I told Gabrielle that Watson is the handsome one, and I saw him smile and twirl his mustache in response.

grounded_facts: Holmes correctly deduces Gabrielle's wedding location by noting her copper ring.
memories.memory_text: I noticed the copper ring on Gabrielle's hand and remarked that it was her wedding ring, then picked it up from the chemistry table and handed it to her, deducing from its material that she was married in the Congo.

grounded_facts: Gabrielle Valladon is formally interviewed by Holmes and Watson, during which she provides her backstory and reveals an attack.
memories.memory_text: I formally interviewed Gabrielle Valladon while she was in my sitting room, during which she shared her backstory and I observed details like her copper wedding ring, and she pointed out a bundle of letters relevant to her case.

grounded_facts: Gabrielle reveals she was attacked with chloroform and thrown into the water while en route to consult Holmes.
memories.memory_text: Gabrielle told me she was attacked with chloroform and thrown into the water while on her way to consult me.

grounded_facts: Holmes has Gabrielle address a letter with an empty sheet inside to be sent to Ashdown Street.
memories.memory_text: I had Gabrielle address a letter to be sent to Ashdown Street, and I placed a blank sheet inside before sealing it.

grounded_facts: Holmes asks Watson for hammer and chisel to break into the skylight.
memories.memory_text: I asked Watson for the hammer and chisel so I could break into the skylight.

grounded_facts: Holmes catches and supports Gabrielle as she is lowered through the skylight, briefly holding her.
memories.memory_text: I caught Gabrielle as she was lowered through the skylight, holding her around the waist to help her down safely.

grounded_facts: Watson helps Gabrielle through the skylight, and Holmes assists her descent; Watson follows shortly after.
memories.memory_text: I saw Watson help Gabrielle through the skylight and watched as he followed me down after handing over the tools.

grounded_facts: Holmes, Watson, and Gabrielle illegally enter the empty shop through the skylight to investigate its purpose.
memories.memory_text: I led the way as we broke in through the rear skylight, entering the empty shop illegally to investigate what was happening inside.

grounded_facts: Watson uncovers a tarpaulin to reveal a large cage containing about a hundred canaries.
memories.memory_text: I saw Watson uncover a large tarpaulin to reveal a cage filled with about a hundred canaries, their sudden fluttering filling the room with noise.

grounded_facts: A postman delivers a letter through the door slot, landing on a dusty floor with unusual tracks.
memories.memory_text: I witnessed a postman deliver a letter through the door slot, which landed on the dusty floor near unusual double tracks that curved back toward the entrance.

grounded_facts: Holmes breaks into the shop by sawing through the iron bars of a skylight, chips away cement, and swings the grill open to enter.
memories.memory_text: I sawed through the iron bars of the skylight, chipped away the cement, swung the grill open, and entered the shop first, later reassembling my tools into a cane.

grounded_facts: Holmes reassembles his tools into a cane, indicating concealment and preparedness.
memories.memory_text: I reassembled my tools into a cane, restoring it for concealment and readiness in case we needed to leave quickly.

grounded_facts: Gabrielle expresses concern about payment, revealing her purse is lost in the Thames.
Gabrielle tells Holmes she cannot pay because her purse is lost in the Thames.
memories.memory_text: Gabrielle told me she couldn't pay because her purse was lost in the Thames, and I understood her concern about the cost.

grounded_facts: Holmes leads Watson and Gabrielle to conceal themselves beside the rear door as the old woman enters.
memories.memory_text: I led Watson and Gabrielle to conceal ourselves beside the rear door just before the old woman entered, ensuring we remained unseen.

grounded_facts: An old woman in a wheelchair enters, uncovers the cage, and feeds the canaries.
memories.memory_text: I observed the old woman in the wheelchair enter the mews, uncover the canary cage with a pulley, and feed the birds from a paper bag and pitcher.

grounded_facts: Carters arrive to collect canaries for transport, part of a larger operation linked to Inverness.
memories.memory_text: I watched two carters arrive, transfer canaries into a small cage lined with a newspaper from Inverness, and drive away with them.

grounded_facts: Carters greet the woman and purchase two dozen canaries.
Two carters arrive and purchase two dozen canaries from the old woman.
memories.memory_text: I saw two carters arrive in a wagon, greet the woman as 'Duchess,' and purchase two dozen canaries, which they transferred into a small cage before leaving.

grounded_facts: An old woman in a wheelchair enters the shop to feed the canaries and maintain the cage.
memories.memory_text: I observed an old woman in a wheelchair enter the shop, feed the canaries, cover the cage, and leave with the letter after locking up.

grounded_facts: Holmes and team notice the newspaper lining the small bird cage is the Inverness Courier, suggesting a location.
memories.memory_text: I noticed the newspaper lining the bottom of the small bird cage had the masthead of the Inverness Courier, which I later mentioned to my companion.

grounded_facts: Gabrielle discovers and hands Holmes a letter delivered to the shop that is addressed to him.
memories.memory_text: I saw Gabrielle notice the letter left on the cage, and she handed it to me, saying, 'It's addressed to you.'

grounded_facts: A letter is delivered to the shop and later retrieved, part of a covert communication system.
memories.memory_text: I saw a letter delivered through the front door slot, later retrieved it from the covered cage, and noticed it was addressed to me.

grounded_facts: Holmes opens and reads a letter from Mycroft summoning him to the Diogenes Club at 11 a.m.
memories.memory_text: I opened the letter and read Mycroft's message summoning me and Watson to the Diogenes Club at 11 a.m.

grounded_facts: Holmes tells Watson to reset his watch after reading Mycroft's letter.
memories.memory_text: I told Watson that either his watch was wrong or Mycroft had miscalculated, and knowing Mycroft, I suggested he reset his watch.

grounded_facts: Watson tells Holmes he is apprehensive about confronting Madame Valladon.
memories.memory_text: Watson told me he was apprehensive about confronting Madame Valladon, and I understood his concern.

grounded_facts: Holmes tells Watson that Madame Valladon is safe with Mrs. Hudson.
memories.memory_text: I told Watson not to worry, that Madame Valladon was perfectly safe with Mrs. Hudson.

grounded_facts: Holmes and Watson visit the Diogenes Club to meet Mycroft.
memories.memory_text: I went to the Diogenes Club with Watson to meet Mycroft.

grounded_facts: Holmes and Watson arrive at the Diogenes Club and begin entering the building.
memories.memory_text: I was ascending the steps of the Diogenes Club with Watson, and I opened the door for us to go in.

grounded_facts: The porter attempts to have Holmes and Watson sign in, but they ignore him and proceed directly upstairs.
memories.memory_text: I heard the porter ask us to sign in, but I ignored him and continued upstairs with Watson, knowing such formalities were unnecessary in this case.

grounded_facts: Holmes observes the ash of a sleeping man's cigar and deduces it is Jamaican, likely Tropical or Golosina.
memories.memory_text: I picked up the ashtray just in time to catch the falling ash from the sleeping man's cigar, and as I put it back, I studied the ash closely — it's Jamaican, I'm sure of that, though I'm not quite certain whether it's from Tropical or Golosina.

grounded_facts: Holmes and Watson enter the Diogenes Club to meet Mycroft Holmes in the upstairs study.
memories.memory_text: I entered the Diogenes Club with Watson to see my brother Mycroft in his upstairs study, and we made our way directly toward the room.

grounded_facts: Mycroft explicitly tells Holmes to cease investigating the engineer case due to national security concerns.
memories.memory_text: Mycroft explicitly told me to cease investigating the engineer case, and I understood it as a direct order to stop my pursuit.

grounded_facts: Mycroft informs Holmes that the engineer case involves national security and is being handled by his organization, implying government authority.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Mycroft that the engineer case involves national security and is being handled by his organization, implying his government authority.

grounded_facts: A private meeting between Mycroft Holmes, Sherlock Holmes, and Dr. Watson in the study of the Diogenes Club.
memories.memory_text: I was in the study of the Diogenes Club with Mycroft and Watson, where I remarked on the waste of precious tobacco, and later observed how the Club seems to be everywhere under the guise of academic pursuits.

grounded_facts: Mycroft receives and responds to a telegram with cryptic instructions, indicating covert operations.
memories.memory_text: I witnessed Mycroft receiving and responding to a telegram with cryptic instructions about sending three boxes to Glennahurich and the red runner to the castle, which suggested covert operations were underway.

grounded_facts: Mycroft explicitly states that his warning is not a suggestion but an order from Her Majesty's government.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Mycroft that his warning was not just a suggestion, but an order from Her Majesty's government, and he made it clear I was expected to obey.

grounded_facts: After the confrontation, Mycroft ends the meeting with formal courtesy.
memories.memory_text: I heard Mycroft end the meeting with formal courtesy, excusing himself from our conversation.

grounded_facts: Mycroft hands back Holmes' cane, calling it a 'tool-kit' in a teasing manner.
memories.memory_text: I caught my cane when Mycroft tossed it back to me, teasing me by calling it my 'tool-kit'.

grounded_facts: Instead of answering Watson's question, Holmes shifts focus by explaining the etymology of 'Glennahurich'.
memories.memory_text: When Watson asked me again if I was dropping the case, I chose not to answer directly and instead redirected him by asking what the word Glennahurich suggested to him.

grounded_facts: Holmes deciphers the meaning of the name 'Glennahurich' as 'Valley of the Yew Tree', suggesting a geographical destination.
memories.memory_text: I explained to Watson that Glennahurich is a Scottish name and breaks down into 'glen' for valley, 'na' for of the, and 'Hurich' meaning yew tree, so together it forms 'Valley of the Yew Tree'.

grounded_facts: Holmes concludes that the three boxes are destined for the Valley of the Yew Tree, based on his interpretation of 'Glennahurich'.
memories.memory_text: I concluded that the three boxes must be destined for the Valley of the Yew Tree based on my interpretation of the name Glennahurich.

grounded_facts: Watson repeatedly asks Holmes whether he is truly dropping the case, showing concern and seeking reassurance.
memories.memory_text: I remember Watson repeatedly asking me whether I was truly dropping the case, clearly concerned and seeking reassurance, even breaking off his singing to press me on it.

grounded_facts: Upon attempting to enter 221B, Holmes and Watson are met with a revolver pointed at them through the door, held by Mrs. Hudson.
memories.memory_text: As Watson and I approached the door of 221B, I was still whistling, but then a revolver appeared through the gap, pointed directly at us, and I realized we were being blocked by someone inside.

grounded_facts: Holmes speaks calmly to Mrs. Hudson to prevent her from shooting, using humor to defuse the situation.
memories.memory_text: I spoke calmly to Mrs. Hudson through the door, telling her not to shoot because she might lose two excellent tenants, using our status as paying lodgers to ease the tension.

grounded_facts: Mrs. Hudson expresses frustration about the absurd difficulty of doing embroidery while holding a gun.
memories.memory_text: I heard Mrs. Hudson complain about how absurd it was to try doing embroidery while holding a gun.

grounded_facts: Holmes informs Mrs. Hudson that the gun she was holding was not loaded, altering her understanding of the risk she faced.
memories.memory_text: I told Mrs. Hudson she'd be relieved to know the gun she was holding was not loaded.

grounded_facts: Watson presses Holmes on whether he intends to disobey Mycroft's orders, emphasizing the political stakes.
memories.memory_text: I remember Watson pressing me on whether I intended to disobey Mycroft's orders, warning me about defying the government, but I said nothing.

grounded_facts: Gabrielle is waiting at the flat's doorway and immediately asks for updates, signaling urgency and her dependence on their investigation.
Gabrielle immediately questions the returning pair for any updates on the investigation.
memories.memory_text: I saw Gabrielle waiting in the doorway of our flat as Watson and I reached the landing, and she immediately asked us, 'Any news? Did you find out anything?'

grounded_facts: Holmes corrects Gabrielle's misunderstanding by revealing the staged nature of her departure.
memories.memory_text: I corrected Gabrielle after she asked if I was sending her back to Brussels, reminding her that I only said we would put her on the boat-train, not that she would stay on it, as she had misunderstood my plan.

grounded_facts: After misunderstanding Holmes's intention, Gabrielle realizes the ruse, thanks him, and apologizes for doubting him.
Gabrielle expresses regret for doubting Holmes and thanks him with a kiss on the cheek.
memories.memory_text: I saw Gabrielle tearfully declare she wouldn't go back to Brussels and would keep searching no matter what, but after I clarified that I never intended for her to stay on the boat-train, she realized my true plan, thanked me, apologized for doubting me, and kissed me on the cheek.

grounded_facts: Holmes informs Gabrielle and Watson that they will stage her departure on the boat-train to Brussels while secretly rerouting to Inverness under assumed identities.
memories.memory_text: I informed Gabrielle and Watson that at 7:30 that evening, we would take her to Victoria Station and put her on the boat-train, but I made it clear to her that she wouldn't stay on it — instead, we would secretly reroute to Inverness under aliases.

grounded_facts: Holmes, Watson, and Gabrielle make arrangements for a covert journey involving staged departures and assumed identities.
memories.memory_text: I told Gabrielle to pack her things and arranged with Watson to take her to Victoria Station that evening, where we would put her on the boat-train to Brussels while ensuring we were seen waving goodbye to Madame Valladon, all part of a covert journey I had planned under assumed identities.

grounded_facts: Gabrielle begins packing and retrieves her belongings, including her missing glove.
memories.memory_text: I saw Gabrielle begin packing and head off to Watson's room, then later return with a glove and check around the window while holding her parasol.

grounded_facts: Watson locates Gabrielle's missing glove after she searches for it.
memories.memory_text: I watched Watson peer under the couch and then emerge with the missing glove, saying, 'Here it is.'

grounded_facts: Holmes deflects Gabrielle's inquiry about being embarrassed by referencing an unusual past experience, maintaining emotional control and shifting conversational focus.
Holmes discloses having spent a night in a harem in Constantinople during a case, introducing new personal history that reframes his relationship with Gabrielle.
memories.memory_text: I deflected Gabrielle's question about whether she was embarrassing me by telling her I once spent a night in a harem in Constantinople during a case, shifting the conversation away from discomfort with something unexpected.

grounded_facts: A private nighttime moment shared between Holmes and Gabrielle in a train sleeping compartment, marked by informal conversation and lowered social barriers.
memories.memory_text: I remember being in the sleeping compartment with Gabrielle at night, changing into my nightshirt while she was under the covers, and later climbing up to the upper berth after speaking with her.

grounded_facts: Gabrielle pushes back against Holmes's sweeping negative judgment of women, attempting to moderate his perspective.
memories.memory_text: I recall Gabrielle interrupting me gently, saying I mustn’t judge all women by those I’ve known, as if she wanted to believe better of her own kind.

grounded_facts: Holmes discloses to Gabrielle that he was once engaged to be married, but the wedding was canceled due to his fiancée's sudden death from influenza one day before the ceremony.
Holmes reveals intimate details about his past romantic life, including a broken engagement due to his fiancée's death, in response to Gabrielle's questioning.
memories.memory_text: I told Gabrielle about my fiancée, the daughter of my violin teacher—we were to be married, the invitations sent, my tail-coat being fitted—when she died of influenza just one day before the wedding.

grounded_facts: After recounting his past engagement and other negative experiences, Holmes concludes that women are unreliable and not to be trusted, reinforcing his earlier stance.
memories.memory_text: After sharing what happened, I told Gabrielle it only proved my point—that women, especially those I’ve been close to, are unreliable and not to be trusted.

grounded_facts: A private, intimate conversation between Holmes and Gabrielle takes place late at night in a train sleeping compartment, during which personal beliefs and histories are shared.
memories.memory_text: I remember that late night in the train compartment, lying in the upper berth while Gabrielle read below; it was dark except for her lamp, and that’s when she challenged me about women, and I ended up telling her things I rarely speak of.

grounded_facts: Holmes, Gabrielle, and Watson arrive at Inverness station as the Highland Express departs.
memories.memory_text: I arrived at Inverness station with Gabrielle and Watson just as the Highland Express was pulling out, the last car vanishing into the steam.

grounded_facts: Holmes asks the baggageman for directions and distance to Glennahurich.
memories.memory_text: I asked the baggageman how to get to Glennahurich and how far it was.

grounded_facts: Watson suggests Glennahurich could be a nice picnic spot, misunderstanding its true nature.
memories.memory_text: I heard Watson suggest that Glennahurich might be a nice place for a picnic if it had a view.

grounded_facts: The group learns that Glennahurich, a destination they are inquiring about, is a cemetery and not suitable for a picnic.
memories.memory_text: I learned from the baggageman that Glennahurich is a cemetery, not a place for picnics.

grounded_facts: The group observes seven cowled Trappist monks, led by von Tirpitz, crossing an iron footbridge over the railway tracks.
memories.memory_text: I saw seven cowled Trappist monks crossing the iron footbridge over the railway tracks, with von Tirpitz leading them.

grounded_facts: Holmes, Gabrielle, and Watson observe a funeral with three coffins and note the absence of mourners and flowers.
A funeral for three unidentified individuals — one adult and two children-sized — takes place with no mourners present.
memories.memory_text: I observed a funeral with Watson and Gabrielle from behind a headstone, noting the three coffins—one adult-sized and two smaller ones—being carried on a cart, and remarked to myself how sad and odd it was that there were no mourners or flowers present.

grounded_facts: Holmes questions the grave-digger about the deceased and the circumstances of their death.
memories.memory_text: I questioned the grave-digger about what had happened to the deceased and the circumstances of their death.

grounded_facts: Holmes questions a grave-digger who reveals the deceased were a father and two sons found floating in the loch, though locals suspect the Loch Ness Monster.
memories.memory_text: I was told by the grave-digger that the deceased were a father and two sons found floating in the loch, though he mentioned locals suspect the Loch Ness Monster.

grounded_facts: Holmes deduces that the four flower-laying 'boys' are actually adult midgets, likely the missing acrobat brothers, and infers the third grave's occupant is unknown.
memories.memory_text: I noticed the small figures laying flowers had the faces of grown men, so I deduced they weren't boys but adult midgets, likely the missing acrobat brothers from the circus, and I realized the third grave's occupant remains unknown to me.

grounded_facts: Four adult midgets, appearing as boys, silently lay flowers on the two small graves and pray.
memories.memory_text: I saw four small figures approaching the graves carrying flowers, and though they appeared at first to be boys, I noticed their mature facial features when they turned their heads, and realized they were adult midgets who silently laid flowers on the two small graves and prayed.

grounded_facts: Holmes raises the unresolved question of who is buried in the third grave, implying the two small graves may not have contained the father's sons.
memories.memory_text: I raised the question of who is buried in the third grave, since the small coffins may not have contained the father's sons after all.

grounded_facts: Gabrielle screams and collapses upon recognizing her husband's body, and is caught by Watson.
memories.memory_text: I saw Gabrielle scream and collapse as she recognized the body, and Watson caught her just in time.

grounded_facts: Holmes confirms the corpse is Emile Valladon based on facial recognition.
memories.memory_text: I confirmed the corpse was Emile Valladon by recognizing his face.

grounded_facts: Watson informs Holmes that Gabrielle has fainted.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Watson that Gabrielle had fainted.

grounded_facts: Holmes asks Watson to hand him the lantern.
memories.memory_text: I asked Watson to hand me the lantern so I could examine the coffin more closely.

grounded_facts: Holmes leads an exhumation at night in Glennahurich Cemetery to inspect the coffin of Emile Valladon.
Holmes pries open the coffin lid, revealing the corpse of Emile Valladon.
memories.memory_text: I led the exhumation at Glennahurich Cemetery at night, and I pried open the coffin lid to reveal the corpse of Emile Valladon, using the lantern Watson passed down to me.

grounded_facts: Holmes notices the green discoloration of Valladon's wedding ring and the presence of three bleached white canaries at his feet.
memories.memory_text: I noticed the wedding ring had turned green and saw three bleached white canaries at the feet of the corpse, which struck me as highly unusual.

grounded_facts: Holmes, Watson, and Gabrielle arrive at the Caledonian Hotel by carriage at dawn.
memories.memory_text: I arrived at the Caledonian Hotel by carriage at dawn with Watson and Gabrielle, and I got out after we stopped.

grounded_facts: Holmes registers under the false name 'Mr. And Mrs. Ashdown and valet, London'.
memories.memory_text: I registered us under the false name 'Mr. And Mrs. Ashdown and valet, London' at the hotel desk.

grounded_facts: The characters arrive at the hotel and are being settled into their rooms at dawn, with the manager assisting in orientation.
memories.memory_text: I arrived at the hotel with Gabrielle and Watson just before dawn, and we were being settled into our rooms with the manager's assistance.

grounded_facts: The manager points out the view of the loch and comments on the morning mist.
memories.memory_text: The manager told me and the others that we had a lovely view of the loch, though the morning mist still shrouded it.

grounded_facts: The manager opens the curtains to reveal the view of the lake and provides a guidebook for sightseeing.
memories.memory_text: I saw the manager open the curtains to reveal the lake view, and then he handed us a guidebook for sightseeing around the area.

grounded_facts: The manager gestures and speaks to Watson, indicating he should follow to his room.
Watson follows the manager out of the room to be shown to his own room.
memories.memory_text: I saw the manager gesture and speak to Watson, indicating he should follow to his room, and then I watched as Watson picked up his suitcase and followed him out.

grounded_facts: Gabrielle tearfully gives her wedding ring to Holmes for comparison.
memories.memory_text: I saw Gabrielle tearfully remove her wedding ring and hand it to me, her emotions clearly overwhelming her in that moment.

grounded_facts: Holmes compares Gabrielle's wedding ring with Valladon's ring in the light, noting a color difference that suggests the cause of death was not drowning.
memories.memory_text: I compared Gabrielle's wedding ring with Valladon's ring in the light, noting a distinct color difference in the copper, which suggested the cause of death was not drowning.

grounded_facts: Holmes tells Gabrielle to stop interrupting so he can continue his investigation.
memories.memory_text: I told Gabrielle to stop interrupting me so I could continue my investigation.

grounded_facts: Holmes conducts a forensic examination of wedding rings to determine the cause of Valladon's death, while managing Gabrielle's emotional state.
memories.memory_text: I conducted a forensic examination of the wedding rings to determine how Valladon died, while managing Gabrielle's emotional state by reminding her of our cover as a couple from London on holiday.

grounded_facts: Holmes tells Gabrielle to stop crying and reminds her of their cover identity, helping her regain composure.
memories.memory_text: I told Gabrielle to stop crying and reminded her that we're the nice couple from London on holiday in the Highlands, and I saw her manage a tentative smile.

grounded_facts: Watson urgently moves from the attic to Holmes' room and opens the door forcefully.
memories.memory_text: I saw Watson come dashing down the narrow stairs from the attic and race toward my door, bursting in with urgency.

grounded_facts: Watson urgently tells Holmes that he saw the monster in the lake from the attic.
Watson claims to have seen the monster from the attic and reports it to Holmes.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Watson that he saw the monster in the lake from the attic and reported it to me.

grounded_facts: Watson asks Holmes about the location of the telescope.
memories.memory_text: I saw Watson ask about the location of the telescope while looking around desperately.

grounded_facts: Watson rushes through the French window to the balcony to look at the lake.
Watson takes a small telescope from Holmes' suitcase.
memories.memory_text: I saw Watson take a small telescope from my suitcase and rush through the French window to the balcony to look at the lake.

grounded_facts: Watson becomes excited and claims to see the monster in the lake through the telescope.
memories.memory_text: I saw Watson become excited and nearly drop the telescope, and he called out to me, 'There it is! There it is!' while claiming to see the monster in the lake.

grounded_facts: Watson hands the telescope to Holmes and urges him to see the monster for himself.
memories.memory_text: Watson handed me the telescope and told me to look for myself, urging me to see the monster on the lake.

grounded_facts: Holmes uses the telescope to look at the lake for signs of the monster, but sees nothing.
memories.memory_text: I used the telescope to examine the lake carefully, but I saw no sign of the monster.

grounded_facts: Holmes and Watson use a telescope from the balcony to observe the lake, searching for a previously sighted object.
memories.memory_text: I lowered the telescope and told Watson I see nothing while we were searching the lake from the balcony.

grounded_facts: Watson takes the telescope from Holmes to look at the lake himself.
memories.memory_text: I witnessed Watson take the telescope from me and look toward the lake himself.

grounded_facts: Watson disputes Holmes' claim of seeing nothing by taking the telescope to verify for himself.
memories.memory_text: I lowered the telescope and said I saw nothing, then Watson questioned me and took it from me to look himself.

grounded_facts: Watson reports that the object he previously saw on the lake is no longer visible.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Watson that the object he had seen was gone.

grounded_facts: Holmes expresses skepticism about the prior existence of the object Watson claims to have seen.
memories.memory_text: I said to Watson, 'Gone? Maybe it was never there,' because I couldn't accept that such an object existed without rational proof.

grounded_facts: Holmes implies Watson may have imagined the object, invoking the rationalist spirit of the century.
memories.memory_text: I told Watson that we are living in the Nineteenth Century, implying he may have imagined the object he claimed to see.

grounded_facts: Holmes steps back into the room, ending his engagement with the outdoor observation.
memories.memory_text: I stepped back into the room, ending my engagement with the outdoor observation, because there was nothing more to see.

grounded_facts: Holmes deduces that Monsieur Valladon did not drown but died of asphyxiation due to chlorine gas exposure, based on evidence from the wedding rings and canary discoloration.
memories.memory_text: I deduced that Monsieur Valladon did not drown but died of asphyxiation from chlorine gas, because I observed that only chlorine gas can turn a copper wedding ring green and bleach the color out of canaries.

grounded_facts: Watson counters Holmes's dismissal of his sighting by pointing out the contradiction in Holmes criticizing him for lacking imagination while now calling his observation a figment.
memories.memory_text: I remember Watson confronting me, saying I called him the least logical man when I dismissed his sighting, and he challenged me by asking how it could be a figment of his imagination if I've always claimed he has none.

grounded_facts: Holmes, Gabrielle, and Watson leave the hotel on bicycles, beginning a journey to investigate castles.
memories.memory_text: I left the hotel on a bicycle with Gabrielle and Watson, beginning our journey to investigate the castles.

grounded_facts: A midday outdoor meal by the lake involving Holmes, Gabrielle, and Watson.
Holmes, Gabrielle, and Watson are having a picnic by the lake, with food spread out and wine being poured.
memories.memory_text: I was sitting on the blanket with Gabrielle and Watson by the lake, our picnic spread out around us while Watson poured the wine.

grounded_facts: Holmes politely asks Watson to pass the cranberry sauce during the picnic.
memories.memory_text: I asked John to pass me the cranberry sauce during our meal.

grounded_facts: Seven Trappist monks appear on the road above, walking in single file toward a bridge over the narrowing lake.
memories.memory_text: I saw seven Trappist monks walking in single file on the road above, approaching a bridge over the narrowing lake.

grounded_facts: Watson calls out and waves to the monks, recognizing them from a previous train ride, but they do not respond.
memories.memory_text: I heard Watson call out and wave to the monks, recognizing them from a previous train ride, but they did not respond.

grounded_facts: Holmes notices Gabrielle manipulating her parasol and asks if something is wrong.
memories.memory_text: I noticed Gabrielle acting strangely with her parasol, so I asked her, 'What is it, dear? What's the matter?'

grounded_facts: Gabrielle notices a bee and begins using her parasol to fend it off by opening and closing it.
memories.memory_text: I saw Gabrielle rapidly opening and closing her parasol, though I didn't know why she was doing it at first.

grounded_facts: Gabrielle challenges Watson's dismissal of the castle by pointing out the presence of security measures, prompting further consideration.
memories.memory_text: I noticed Gabrielle challenge Watson's dismissal of the castle by pointing out the security measures, which reinforced my own assessment.

grounded_facts: A brief observational visit by Holmes, Gabrielle, and Watson to Urquhart Castle during daylight, intended to assess access but aborted due to security measures.
Holmes, Gabrielle, and Watson arrive by bicycle at the gates of Urquhart Castle and observe warning signs and a guard, leading to their decision to leave the main entrance.
memories.memory_text: I arrived by bicycle with Gabrielle and Watson at Urquhart Castle, where we saw warning signs and a guard approaching with mastiffs, so I decided we should leave the main entrance and look elsewhere.

grounded_facts: Holmes decides to bypass the main entrance after being deterred by the guard and warning sign, opting instead to find an alternative way in.
memories.memory_text: I chose to bypass the main entrance because the guard and warning sign made it clear access was restricted, so I resolved to find another way in.

grounded_facts: Holmes explains to Watson that since they cannot enter through the front, they will attempt entry via a tradesman's entrance.
memories.memory_text: I told Watson that since we couldn't enter through the front, we would try the tradesman's entrance instead.

grounded_facts: Holmes engages the guide in a discussion about the historical origins of Urquhart Castle to test his knowledge.
memories.memory_text: I engaged the guide in conversation to test his knowledge, asking him whether Urquhart Castle was built under James the Second or James the Third.

grounded_facts: Holmes realizes the guide incorrectly dated Urquhart Castle's construction, identifying it as 1500 under James the Fourth instead of the guide's claim of 1400 under James the Third.
memories.memory_text: I realized the guide had incorrectly dated the castle's construction, claiming it was under James the Third in 1400, when I know it was actually under James the Fourth in 1500, as confirmed by my guidebook.

grounded_facts: Holmes, Watson, and Gabrielle observe workmen transporting a birdcage and crates labeled 'SULPHURIC ACID - CORROSIVE' into the castle tower.
memories.memory_text: I saw the workmen carry a birdcage and crates labeled 'SULPHURIC ACID - CORROSIVE' into the castle tower while Watson and Gabrielle were with me.

grounded_facts: Holmes deduces that the combination of sulphuric acid and saltwater could be used to generate chlorine gas, indicating a dangerous or malicious operation.
memories.memory_text: I realized that if sulphuric acid is exposed to saltwater, it could produce chlorine gas—it made sense to me as a graduate chemist.

grounded_facts: Holmes asks Watson to clasp his hands to serve as a step for climbing scaffolding.
memories.memory_text: I asked Watson to clasp his hands so I could use them as a step to climb the scaffolding.

grounded_facts: Holmes, Watson, and Gabrielle arrive at Urquhart Castle intending to tour the site, but instead observe suspicious restoration activities.
memories.memory_text: I arrived at Urquhart Castle with Watson and Gabrielle intending to tour the site, but instead I noticed suspicious restoration activities, including workmen handling a birdcage and crates marked 'SULPHURIC ACID - CORROSIVE'.

grounded_facts: Watson signals discomfort and fear upon seeing the guard's aggressive mastiffs.
memories.memory_text: I saw Watson cast anxious glances over his shoulder as we fled, clearly uneasy about the aggressive mastiffs barking behind us.

grounded_facts: After observing suspicious activity and being noticed by guard dogs, Holmes leads Watson and Gabrielle in a swift departure from Urquhart Castle.
memories.memory_text: I led Watson and Gabrielle in a swift departure from Urquhart Castle after we were noticed by the guard dogs, knowing we had to avoid confrontation.

grounded_facts: When Watson jumps up upon seeing the monster, Holmes grabs his arm and pulls him back to prevent panic and maintain control.
memories.memory_text: When Watson jumped up shouting 'Holmes!', I grabbed his arm and pulled him back into his seat to keep him from panicking and capsizing us before we even began the pursuit.

grounded_facts: Holmes asks Watson for his stethoscope to listen for underwater activity after the monster submerges.
memories.memory_text: I asked Watson for his stethoscope, and he handed it to me after removing it from his hat.

grounded_facts: Holmes uses Watson's stethoscope to detect mechanical sounds beneath the water, indicating artificial origin of the monster.
memories.memory_text: I used the stethoscope underwater and heard something mechanical, which made me suspect the monster was artificial.

grounded_facts: The creature is spotted moving through the mist on Loch Ness, approaching the boat before submerging and later resurfacing nearby, causing the boat to capsize.
memories.memory_text: I saw the monster moving toward us through the mist, its long neck cutting through the water until it submerged; moments later, it resurfaced nearby and Watson threw an oar at it, which caused our boat to capsize and threw me into the lake.

grounded_facts: The monster passes close to the boat, creating a backwash that rocks it broadside and throws all three occupants into the lake.
memories.memory_text: I was rowing the boat to intercept the monster when it passed close by, and the backwash from its movement rocked the vessel so violently that Watson, Gabrielle, and I were all thrown into the lake.

grounded_facts: Watson compares his fear of the monster to past dangers in India, stating he was never half as frightened.
memories.memory_text: I heard Watson say he wasn't half as frightened facing man-eating tigers or wild elephants in India as he was by this beast, and that the monster seemed to have a personal grudge against us.

grounded_facts: After the monster disappears, the wooden scaffolding in front of the castle tower rises into the air, then descends again, suggesting a hidden mechanism connected to the monster.
memories.memory_text: I saw the wooden scaffolding in front of the castle tower rise into the air after the monster vanished, as the mist briefly lifted.

grounded_facts: Holmes, Watson, and Gabrielle observe Urquhart Castle from a rowboat and attempt to intercept the Loch Ness Monster after spotting it in the lake.
memories.memory_text: I was in the rowboat with Watson and Gabrielle, watching Urquhart Castle through the mist when we spotted the creature in the lake; I took up my oar and we began rowing to intercept it before it vanished.

grounded_facts: Holmes explains that the monster likely returned to the castle for 'supper', implying it is mechanical and operated from within the structure.
memories.memory_text: I told Watson that the monster likely returned to the castle for supper, implying it is mechanical and operated from within.

grounded_facts: Watson asks Holmes if he wants to confide, noting that whistling usually means he's close to a solution.
memories.memory_text: I noticed Watson asked if I wanted to confide, and he mentioned that my whistling means I'm close to a solution, which I often do when the pieces are falling into place.

grounded_facts: Holmes draws a parallel between the case and the ballet 'Swan Lake', suggesting deception in form (swan/monster).
memories.memory_text: I thought about how the monster in the lake is like the swan in 'Swan Lake'—a deception in form, not truly what it appears to be.

grounded_facts: Holmes, Watson, and Gabrielle discuss the nature of the monster and the conspiracy while in a hotel room at night.
memories.memory_text: I was pacing in the hotel room while Watson warmed himself by the fire and Gabrielle watched from the bed, and I realized we were dealing with a mechanical monster.

grounded_facts: Holmes concludes that the creature in the lake is a mechanical construct with an artificial heart and lungs, based on auditory evidence and observed bubbles.
memories.memory_text: I concluded that the creature in the lake must be a mechanical construct with an engine for a heart, based on the sounds I heard through the stethoscope and how well water carries sound.

grounded_facts: Holmes confirms that Gabrielle's husband was involved in the mechanical monster scheme.
memories.memory_text: I confirmed to Madame Valladon that I was sure her husband was involved in the scheme.

grounded_facts: Holmes reveals that the Society for the Preservation of Scottish Monuments, i.e., the Diogenes Club, is behind the operation.
memories.memory_text: I revealed to the others that I had figured out the Society for the Preservation of Scottish Monuments—better known as the Diogenes Club—was behind the operation.

grounded_facts: A manager delivers a magnum of champagne to Holmes under mysterious instructions, signaling the beginning of the final confrontation.
memories.memory_text: I remember that A manager delivers a magnum of champagne to Holmes under mysterious instructions, signaling the beginning of the final confrontation.

grounded_facts: Watson offers a revolver to Holmes for protection before his departure.
Watson offers a revolver for protection, but Holmes ignores it and exits.
memories.memory_text: Watson offered me a revolver for protection, saying 'You'd better take this with you,' but I ignored it and left, knowing I wouldn't need it.

grounded_facts: The guide reveals that Jonah is hosting the party Holmes is being taken to.
memories.memory_text: I asked the guide who the host was, and he told me it was Jonah.

grounded_facts: An upcoming gathering hosted by Jonah, expected to have an impressive guest list.
memories.memory_text: I was told that Jonah is hosting the party and that I won't be disappointed by the guest list.

grounded_facts: Holmes leaves the Caledonian Hotel in a gig accompanied by the guide.
memories.memory_text: I left the Caledonian Hotel in a gig with the guide, and I remember the horse starting off at a trot as we turned into the driveway.

grounded_facts: Holmes dismounts from the gig and walks up the steps to the inner courtyard, marked by a red carpet.
memories.memory_text: I dismounted from the gig and walked up the steps, examining the red carpet as I went.

grounded_facts: Mycroft greets Holmes by pretending to mistake him for 'Mr. Ashdown', to which Holmes responds with a similar ironic remark about the red carpet.
memories.memory_text: I saw Mycroft step out from one of the tents, and when he greeted me as 'Mr. Ashdown,' I replied with a smile, 'The red runner, I presume.'

grounded_facts: Mycroft asks Holmes to hand over the champagne bottle, which Holmes does, commenting on its quality.
memories.memory_text: I handed over the champagne bottle when Mycroft asked for it, and I remarked that it was mediocre, though not meant for drinking.

grounded_facts: Mycroft requests and receives a bottle of champagne from Holmes, which he then hands to a man in black for ceremonial use.
memories.memory_text: I saw Mycroft take the champagne from me and give it to a man in black, so I know it was intended for ceremonial use.

grounded_facts: Mycroft calls out to McKeller and instructs him to tie up the champagne bottle.
memories.memory_text: I inferred that Mycroft must have instructed McKeller to secure the champagne, since I heard him call out and later saw the man in black take it before being told to tie it up.

grounded_facts: Workmen are preparing the castle grounds with torches and a red carpet; Mycroft oversees arrangements involving symbolic use of champagne.
memories.memory_text: I noticed workmen lighting torches and unrolling a red carpet across the courtyard, and saw Mycroft overseeing the arrangements, handing over a bottle of champagne with instructions to tie it up before stepping back into the tent.

grounded_facts: Holmes enters the tent at Mycroft's invitation, marking the transition into a private interaction space.
Mycroft pulls back the tent flap and tells Holmes to enter, signaling the start of a private interaction.
memories.memory_text: I entered the tent after Mycroft pulled back the flap and told me, 'In here,' marking the start of our private conversation.

grounded_facts: Mycroft tells Holmes that his investigation has unknowingly served the German government.
Holmes is told that his investigation was orchestrated by the German government using Ilse as bait, making him an unwitting agent.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Mycroft that my investigation had been manipulated by the German government, who used Ilse as bait, making me an unwitting agent working for them.

grounded_facts: Mycroft reveals that E. Valladon died in a failed submersible test, and that the British government is developing a secret underwater craft.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Mycroft that E. Valladon died during a failed submersible test in Moray Firth, where seawater mixed with acid batteries and produced deadly chlorine gas, and that the British government is secretly developing an underwater craft.

grounded_facts: Holmes is informed that the woman claiming to be Gabrielle Valladon is actually Ilse von Hoffmanstal, a German agent.
Mycroft informs Holmes that the woman he rescued is not Gabrielle Valladon but Ilse von Hoffmanstal, a German agent.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Mycroft that the woman I rescued, who claimed to be Gabrielle Valladon, is actually Ilse von Hoffmanstal, a German agent.

grounded_facts: A secret meeting in a tent where Mycroft reveals classified information about a failed submersible project and German espionage to Holmes.
memories.memory_text: I was present in the tent when Mycroft revealed to me that I had been manipulated into working for the German government, and during that meeting I saw him open the trunk to show what he claimed was Gabrielle Valladon, while I examined Ilse's water-soaked parasol.

grounded_facts: Queen Victoria arrives by coach at the castle courtyard, marking the beginning of the ceremonial event.
memories.memory_text: I saw the Queen arrive by coach at the castle courtyard, and Mycroft went down the steps to greet her.

grounded_facts: The Queen expresses dissatisfaction with her journey, setting a tone of expectation for the event's significance.
memories.memory_text: I heard the Queen say her journey was long and tedious, and that it had better be worth her while.

grounded_facts: Mycroft formally presents the scientific team responsible for the submersible to the Queen.
Mycroft presents key scientists involved in the submersible project to Queen Victoria, who acknowledges their work.
memories.memory_text: I stood beside Mycroft as he presented the scientists responsible for the submersible to the Queen, introducing Ferguson and Prescott, and I saw them bow as they were acknowledged.

grounded_facts: A formal ceremony hosted by Mycroft to present and inaugurate a new submersible vessel in the presence of Queen Victoria and the scientific team.
memories.memory_text: I stood beside Mycroft when he introduced me to the Queen, and I told her my case was negligible, while she addressed the scientific team about the significance of the new submersible vessel.

grounded_facts: Queen Victoria acknowledges Sherlock Holmes personally, expressing familiarity with his detective work.
memories.memory_text: I was acknowledged by Queen Victoria, who said she had been following my exploits with great interest, and I bowed and thanked her.

grounded_facts: The Queen shows personal interest in Holmes's detective cases, indicating prior awareness of his reputation.
memories.memory_text: I recall the Queen showing personal interest in my current case, asking when we might expect Dr. Watson's account, and I told her I hoped it would never be published because it hasn't been one of my more successful endeavors.

grounded_facts: The royal party, led by Mycroft, proceeds from the courtyard toward the tower where the submersible is housed.
memories.memory_text: I followed the royal party as Mycroft led the Queen toward the tower, crossing the inner courtyard and passing over the drawbridge while the Highland piper briefly preceded us.

grounded_facts: A formal presentation of the H.M.S. Jonah submarine to Queen Victoria and her entourage, including a demonstration of its systems and capabilities.
memories.memory_text: I witnessed the formal presentation of the H.M.S. Jonah to Queen Victoria, where Mycroft demonstrated its systems inside the submarine while the midget crew operated the machinery and canaries chirped overhead.

grounded_facts: Queen Victoria refuses to approve the commissioning of H.M.S. Jonah as a warship, deeming it unsportsmanlike and un-English, and orders it to be scuttled.
The Queen directly criticizes the submarine project to Mycroft, calling it unsportsmanlike and un-English, and orders its destruction.
memories.memory_text: I heard Queen Victoria declare the submarine project unsportsmanlike and un-English, and I saw her order Mycroft to destroy it, expressing her dismay at what scientists might think of next.

grounded_facts: After the Queen's rejection, Mycroft suggests giving the submarine to the Germans as a trap, luring them aboard before sinking it to destroy them.
memories.memory_text: I remember that After the Queen's rejection, Mycroft suggests giving the submarine to the Germans as a trap, luring them aboard before sinking it to destroy them.

grounded_facts: Holmes arrives at the Caledonian Hotel in a gig at dawn and enters the building.
memories.memory_text: I arrived at the Caledonian Hotel in a gig at dawn and walked in, twirling Gabrielle's parasol in my hand.

grounded_facts: Holmes enters the hotel room at dawn, carrying the parasol, indicating his return from an absence.
memories.memory_text: I entered the hotel room at dawn, carrying the parasol, returning after being away.

grounded_facts: Holmes uses the parasol to adjust Gabrielle's slipping negligee while she sleeps, conveying detachment mixed with subtle attention.
Holmes looks at Gabrielle while she sleeps and subtly adjusts her negligee with the parasol, indicating restrained care or control.
memories.memory_text: I looked down at Gabrielle as she slept and used the tip of the parasol to adjust her negligee, keeping my distance while ensuring her modesty.

grounded_facts: Holmes moves to the French window, opens it, and looks outside, establishing a visual connection to the external scene.
memories.memory_text: I moved to the French window, opened it, and glanced out to see what was beyond.

grounded_facts: Holmes sees the monks watching the hotel from the lakefront, establishing mutual observation and potential threat.
From Holmes' perspective, seven Trappist monks are seen standing on the shore, watching the hotel at dawn, suggesting surveillance or symbolic presence.
memories.memory_text: I saw seven Trappist monks standing on the shore, silhouetted against the water at dawn, watching the hotel, and I knew we were being observed.

grounded_facts: Holmes presents the parasol to Gabrielle as a signaling device, inviting her to transmit the message.
memories.memory_text: I handed Gabrielle her parasol and suggested she use it to signal the monks, asking if she'd let them know where to find the submersible.

grounded_facts: Holmes uses linguistic questioning and implied urgency to compel Gabrielle to reveal the correct German phrase.
memories.memory_text: I questioned Gabrielle about the German phrase for 'under the castle,' pressing her with urgency about the waiting monks and the cold morning, and when she hesitated, I handed her the damp parasol and urged her to signal the submersible's location.

grounded_facts: Holmes confirms the German phrase 'unter dem Schloss' as the location clue for the submersible.
memories.memory_text: I confirmed the German phrase 'unter dem Schloss' as the location clue for the submersible after questioning Gabrielle and, when she refused to cooperate, sent the message myself using the parasol to signal in Morse code.

grounded_facts: Holmes uses Gabrielle's parasol to send the message 'UNTER DEM SCHLOSS' in Morse code from the hotel window.
memories.memory_text: I used Gabrielle's parasol myself to send the message 'UNTER DEM SCHLOSS' in Morse code from the hotel window, keeping to the side as I flashed the signals outside.

grounded_facts: A coordinated signaling event from the hotel room to the lakefront monks at dawn, using Morse code via a parasol.
memories.memory_text: I stood to the side of the hotel window and used the parasol to send a Morse code signal toward the lakefront monks at dawn, flashing the message 'UNTER DEM SCHLOSS' to coordinate the location of the submersible.

grounded_facts: Holmes finishes sending a message using the parasol and withdraws it into the room.
memories.memory_text: I finished sending the message with the parasol, closed it, and pulled it back into the room.

grounded_facts: The monks, led by von Tirpitz, turn away from the hotel and walk along the shore.
memories.memory_text: I saw the monks, with von Tirpitz leading, turn away from the hotel and walk off along the shore.

grounded_facts: Gabrielle corrects Holmes's use of her name, asserting her full aristocratic surname 'von Hoffmanstal', indicating a shift in identity disclosure.
memories.memory_text: I remember Gabrielle correcting me about her name, insisting it was 'von Hoffmanstal'—not just 'Hoffmanstal'—which made me realize she was asserting her full aristocratic identity.

grounded_facts: Holmes initially misnames Gabrielle as 'Hoffmanstal', then accepts correction when she specifies 'von Hoffmanstal'.
memories.memory_text: I called her 'Fraulein Hoffmanstal' at first, then I asked 'It isn't?' when she objected, and I accepted her correction by saying 'I stand corrected.'

grounded_facts: Holmes discloses that the Trappist monks will be allowed to take the submersible, which is part of a larger plan leading to their capture at sea.
memories.memory_text: I told Gabrielle that we would let the monks take the submersible, set and running, expecting them to sail it out to meet a German battleship at sea.

grounded_facts: Gabrielle expresses doubt about Holmes’s plan, particularly the idea of letting the monks take the submersible, highlighting potential flaws.
memories.memory_text: Gabrielle questioned me, asking if I meant to let the monks have the submersible, and then pressed with doubt when I mentioned they would try to escape, clearly skeptical of the plan's risks.

grounded_facts: Upon Holmes's instruction, Gabrielle begins packing her belongings in anticipation of Mycroft arriving to take her into custody.
memories.memory_text: I told Gabrielle to get her things together because Mycroft would be arriving to take her into custody, and I saw her begin packing her clothes from the wardrobe.

grounded_facts: A final exchange between Holmes and Gabrielle in a hotel room at dawn, following the completion of her espionage mission, where identities are clarified, plans revealed, and custody arranged.
memories.memory_text: I recall stepping back from the window to face Gabrielle at dawn in the hotel room, where we had a final exchange after her mission ended—she revealed she had sought me out as the best, I let her know Mycroft would take her into custody, and we clarified the plan with the monks and the air-pump.

grounded_facts: Gabrielle admits she sought the assignment to challenge Holmes, acknowledges her defeat, and expresses regret at not providing stronger opposition.
Gabrielle confesses she failed and regrets not offering Holmes a better challenge, revealing vulnerability.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Gabrielle that she had sought the assignment specifically to challenge me, admitting she failed and regretting she didn't provide a stronger game, and when I replied 'Close enough,' she seemed to accept it with a quiet vulnerability.

grounded_facts: Watson, now dressed again in his valet outfit, rushes from the attic down the narrow stairs toward Holmes' room.
memories.memory_text: I saw Watson come bounding down the narrow stairs from the attic, racing toward my room while back in his valet's outfit.

grounded_facts: Watson shouts Holmes' name repeatedly upon arriving at the door of his room, indicating urgency.
memories.memory_text: I heard Watson shout my name urgently at the door of my room, calling out 'Holmes! Holmes!' as he approached.

grounded_facts: Watson bursts into the hotel room in haste, trips over Gabrielle's bag, and falls, then begins to get back up.
memories.memory_text: I saw Watson burst into the room in a hurry and trip over Gabrielle's bag, falling to the floor before starting to get back up.

grounded_facts: Gabrielle points toward the balcony, likely directing Watson's attention after he falls.
memories.memory_text: I noticed Gabrielle point toward the balcony as Watson was getting up, likely trying to direct his attention.

grounded_facts: Watson excitedly tells Holmes that he saw the creature again, coming from the castle and now in the loch.
Watson urgently informs Holmes that he has again seen the mysterious entity emerging from the castle, now present in the loch.
memories.memory_text: I remember Watson telling me urgently that he saw the creature again, coming from the castle and now in the loch.

grounded_facts: Holmes tells Watson that whatever was out there is now gone forever and invites him to verify it visually.
memories.memory_text: I told Watson that whatever was out there is now gone forever and invited him to look for himself to confirm it.

grounded_facts: The christening champagne bottle and a Bible surface from the water of Loch Ness, indicating something significant has risen or been released from below.
memories.memory_text: I saw the christening champagne bottle and a Bible surface from the water of Loch Ness, rising up after a great turbulence.

grounded_facts: Holmes identifies the bottle of champagne and the Bible as the only remaining items from H.M.S. Jonah, indicating the ship's destruction or loss.
memories.memory_text: I identified the bottle of champagne and the Bible as the only remaining items from H.M.S. Jonah, knowing they were all that was left after the ship's loss.

grounded_facts: Holmes tells Watson that only a bottle of champagne and a Bible remain from H.M.S. Jonah, providing new information that shifts Watson's understanding.
memories.memory_text: I told Watson that only a bottle of champagne and a Bible remain from H.M.S. Jonah, seeing his puzzled reaction as he processed the news.

grounded_facts: Gabrielle is informed she will not be imprisoned but instead exchanged at the Swiss-German border for a British agent, Ibbetson.
Mycroft informs Gabrielle that she will be exchanged at the border rather than imprisoned.
memories.memory_text: I heard Mycroft tell Gabrielle she would be exchanged at the Swiss-German border for a British agent named Ibbetson instead of being imprisoned.

grounded_facts: Mycroft tells Gabrielle that the exchange plan was Holmes's idea.
memories.memory_text: I learned from Mycroft that he credited me with the idea for the exchange, telling Gabrielle it was my plan.

grounded_facts: Holmes gallantly acknowledges Gabrielle's superiority, comparing her favorably to British operatives and even himself.
memories.memory_text: I acknowledged that Gabrielle was better than some consulting detectives, including perhaps myself, during our final exchange.

grounded_facts: A formal handover and farewell event where Gabrielle is escorted out of the hotel by Mycroft and his aide for repatriation.
memories.memory_text: I witnessed the formal handover when Mycroft and his aide escorted Gabrielle out of the hotel for repatriation, and I saw her say goodbye before she walked out with Mycroft following.

grounded_facts: Holmes decides not to publicize Gabrielle's identity and actions, citing her disinterest in media exposure.
memories.memory_text: I decided not to publicize Gabrielle's story because I don't think she'd want it spread across the Strand Magazine.

grounded_facts: Watson questions Holmes's choice to keep Gabrielle's story private, arguing for public transparency.
memories.memory_text: I remember Watson pressing me, saying the public has a right to know and asking why we should care about her feelings if she's a German spy.

grounded_facts: Watson asks Holmes to explain what is happening, offering his loyalty as friend and valet.
memories.memory_text: Watson asked me to explain what's happening, offering his loyalty as my friend and valet, but I told him to be quiet so I could concentrate.

grounded_facts: Holmes focuses on reading a personal message from the carriage scene, indicating new information is being processed.
memories.memory_text: I need to focus on reading this personal message; it contains important information that I must interpret without distraction.

grounded_facts: Holmes translates what the woman outside is saying as 'Auf Wiedersehn', marking a moment of recognition or irony.
